correctness.rationale: Every pairwise distance is at most two due to the universal vertex. Triangle-freeness makes a three-rim geodesic exactly an induced P3 in one component; apex-containing faces are precisely the cone over disjoint graph components, proving GP=A∪_B CB. Each D2(H_i) has complete one-skeleton and is connected; m≥2 makes A simply connected. Maps of all connected graph components B_i into A are nullhomotopic, and a common target point is chosen, so the inclusion B→A is null. Mapping-cone invariance yields A∨ΣB; the unreduced suspension of m connected graph components gives m−1 circles and their sum of cycle ranks two-spheres. D2(C4)=K4 one-skeleton has rank three in H1, and joins of m such wedge-three-circles complexes produce 3^m spheres of dimension 2m−1. Replayed finite checker in its actual package path confirms 7 exact distance and boundary examples, with five additional exact non-cycle-factor tests; the infinite proof is not inferred from the census.

value.rationale: The theorem determines the complete homotopy type of a natural broad universal-apex graph class in terms of established two-independence functors, including explicit nonzero fundamental-group rank, one two-sphere for each internal rim cycle, and a join factor capturing arbitrary higher topology. The natural all-square family yields simultaneously nonzero integral homology in degrees one, two, and 2m−1 and exactly 3^m top sphere generators; this exponential structural behavior cannot be recovered as a homotopy invariant from previous general-position face polynomials without the new attaching-map computation. It is a structural transfer, not a parameter-renaming or isolated small census.
